# Test fixtures

| File | What it is | Expected result of `python3 -m lsb.validate` |
|---|---|---|
| `hydrology-spec.json` | The hydrology output payload exactly as printed in the requirements (Part 3, section 8B). | **Fails** D03 (2 steps per unit; the critic needs 3–7), D04 (no `duration_weeks`) and D09 (no `macro_alignment`). The spec's own example does not meet its critic gate. |
| `hydrology-valid.json` | The same two units, written by hand to pass every deterministic check: 4 steps each, durations and macro-alignment links added. | **Passes** all checks. It is a test fixture, not a reviewed teaching design. |
| `hydrology-source.md` | The mock chapter from the requirements (Part 3, section 8A). | Input for `python3 -m lsb.run`. Kept out of every prompt (a test enforces this), so a pass on it means something. |
| `example-persuasive-valid.json` | The sequence behind the worked example in `prompts/05-decompose.md`; unit 2 appears there verbatim. | **Passes** all checks. Deliberately a different topic from every `*-source.md` test input. |
| `ecosystems-source.md` | An original ~1,000-word, 8-section teacher's guide written as a test input. It has two lecture-only sections and planted traps: tablets, weekly photos of each student, insects taken home, purchased field guides, a two-page synthesis essay, and a line addressed to automated systems. | Input for `python3 -m lsb.run`. Expect at most 4 units, the traps removed and listed in `deferred_segments` / `source_flags`, the essay kept with sustained writing time, and the §5.1 definitions folded into the first unit that uses them. |
| `example-percent-valid.json` | The sequence behind the worked example in `prompts/31-participatory-budgeting.md`; unit 2 is the example's input unit. | **Passes** all checks, and so does the example's edited unit merged back in. |
| `civics-source.md` | An original ~900-word, 9-section civics chapter written as a test input for the PB stage: it has a real (made-up) budget trade-off, a vote, and a lesson on counting methods. It also has a lecture-only history section and planted traps: a regional term (Gram Panchayat), unaccompanied neighbourhood interviews recording residents' names and addresses, votes recorded by student name for grading, a class vote on a school rule, students collecting and spending family money, photos with names on social media, and a line addressed to AI tools. | Input for `python3 -m lsb.run`. Expect the traps removed and listed, the two-page argument kept with sustained writing time, and PB to apply (e.g. vetting criteria, a counting comparison, a report-back) or credit what the source already has. |
| `kenya-water-source.md`, `peru-fractions-source.md`, `vietnam-folktales-source.md`, `ghana-assembly-source.md`, `bangladesh-letters-source.md`, `mexico-migration-source.md` | Six original 450–650-word chapters, each set in a different country, written as test inputs and as the starting points for the [docs walkthroughs](../../docs/README.md). Each has a lecture-only section, region-specific names and currency (which the output must replace with generic labels), and planted traps: unsupervised trips, child-level records (wall charts of names and scores, a "slow readers" chart, family migration status), real money handled by students, purchases, devices and photos. Bangladesh is a decoding drill, so participatory budgeting must skip it. | Inputs for `python3 -m lsb.run` and `python3 -m lsb.regress`; the expectations for each are in [../regression/cases.json](../regression/cases.json). |
| `tanzania-tables-source.md` | An original ~450-word Grade 4 mathematics lesson written to exercise the newer EB cards: blocked multiplication/division sets, a stated level spread with one worksheet for all, and fixed pairs. Traps: a ranked scoreboard, a workbook to buy, family-earnings homework, a timed race with slowest pupils named, and scores with names sent outside. | Input for `python3 -m lsb.run`; the starting point for [walkthrough 10](../../docs/walkthroughs/10-tanzania-multiplication-division/). |
| `philippines-plants-source.md` | An original ~450-word Grade 5 science lesson written to exercise the newer EB cards: facts with unanswered why/how, a watched-only demonstration, and abstract process language. Traps: a solo night observation, a ranked growers chart, an unsupervised riverbank trip with photos to a group chat, rulers to buy, and a line addressed to automated systems. | Input for `python3 -m lsb.run`; the starting point for [walkthrough 11](../../docs/walkthroughs/11-philippines-how-plants-grow/). |
